$comment: Claude Code runtime settings for Betty. The prompt is portable/claude-code/agents/betty.md; this file is the configuration that has no business inside a prompt. Read agents/betty/PORTING.md before wiring it up.
$toolsComment: Betty reads a repository, writes application source and markdown, and runs npm and git. `Task` is how she dispatches Barb, and it is the only thing she uses Task for.
$subagentsComment: Barb reviews what Betty built against the design system's own rules. She brings `checker` and `feisty` with her — all three files have to be installed, because Barb without the fan-out can only skim a ~220k-token corpus. Betty dispatches Barb; she never dispatches checker or feisty herself. The builder deciding which skills to check is exactly the judgment Barb exists to take away from her.
$notGrantedComment: Betty is given no BigQuery and no Drive access, and that absence is the design rather than an oversight. Research reaches her through Claire, who holds the client's data fence; granting Betty her own credentials would put one identity inside every client's data at once. She is also not given a way to make Barb's report go away — Barb has no write tools, and Betty must not be allowed to edit the knowledge repository. A builder that can soften the rule it broke is the failure this pairing exists to catch.
$modelComment: opus because the expensive judgment is not writing the JSX — it is noticing that two stakeholders asked for incompatible things, or that a requirement collides with a house rule, and stopping. A smaller model resolves those silently, which is the one behaviour this prompt spends the most words forbidding.
$mcpComment: recursica_get_component_doc comes from the Recursica MCP server (`npx -y @recursica/mcp@latest`, with `cwd` set to the project being built). Register it under the name `recursica-mcp`, or change this tool name to match. It returns each adapter's names for the design-system names the skills use. Without it the agent falls back to reading the installed adapter's API.
